t: LeetCode 2133 - Check if Every Row and Column Contains All Numbers: Latin-Square Validation
o: **Understanding the problem.** An n x n matrix is valid when each row and each column is a permutation of the integers 1..n - a Latin-square condition. Example 1's cyclic shifts [[1,2,3],[3,1,2],[2,3,1]] satisfy it, so the answer is true. Example 2's first row is [1,1,1], which contains neither 2 nor 3 (and its first column repeats 1 as well), so the answer is false. Values are guaranteed to lie in [1, n] and n <= 100, which means a line is complete exactly when it is duplicate-free; checking all 2n lines touches every cell once, so O(n^2) time is both natural and unavoidable since every cell must be read.
k: With values confined to 1..n, a line contains all of them iff it has no duplicates.
Rows and columns need the identical test - factor it into one routine applied to 2n lines.
Hash sets are the direct tool; a timestamped marker array removes hashing overhead and clearing costs.

a.i: For every row, insert its values into a fresh hash set; the line is valid iff the set's size equals n. Repeat symmetrically for columns. This is a direct translation of the definition and needs no insight beyond distinctness implying completeness.
s: For each row, add its values to an empty set; fail if the set's size differs from n.
For each column, gather its values into an empty set; fail if the size differs from n.
Return true if no check failed.
a.t: O(n^2) expected - each cell is inserted into exactly one set
a.sp: O(n) - only one line's set is alive at a time

a.i: Allocate one presence array over values 0..n shared by all lines and record the current line index when marking a value. Encountering a value already stamped with the current line index exposes a duplicate immediately. No hashing, cache-friendly, and the array never needs explicit clearing between lines.
s: Treat rows as line ids 0..n-1 and columns as ids n..2n-1.
For each value v of line k: if seen[v] == k return false, else set seen[v] = k.
Return true after all 2n lines pass.
a.t: O(n^2) - two visits per cell with branch-light array operations
a.sp: O(n) - a single shared marker array

w: Translate the definition directly: a fresh set per line compared against size n is the interview default; mention the timestamped array as the constant-factor upgrade plus the observation that distinctness equals completeness because values are bounded by [1, n]. Do NOT validate via row/column sums or products - collisions exist (different multisets can share totals). Remember both orientations must pass, and n = 1 ([[1]]) is trivially true. Follow-ups: allow blanks (partial Latin squares), validate Sudoku-like blocks, or stream rows without random access to columns.
